verdict.label: MALICIOUS
verdict.recommended_posture: Queue for analyst review this shift. Quarantine pending a decision.

deterministic_floors.reason: combines a payment instruction, a demand for secrecy and executive or time pressure -- the standard BEC structure

attack_vector.name: Business Email Compromise / payment fraud
attack_vector.description: Impersonates an executive, supplier or internal finance contact to redirect a payment, payroll deposit or gift-card purchase. Usually carries no link or attachment, which defeats URL and sandbox controls.

severity_breakdown.formula: 100 x intent x (0.5 x impact + 0.3 x exploitability + 0.2 x targeting) + escalators

exploitability_signals.reason: gives a concrete payment or banking instruction

targeting_signals.reason: is framed as a reply rather than a cold approach
asks the recipient to keep the request off the record

escalators.name: thread hijack
escalators.reason: injected into what looks like an existing thread, which borrows the trust of the real correspondents

lowering.claim: Quoted material suggesting an existing thread lowered the score

why_flagged.wording_signal: Phrasing most associated with hostile mail in the training corpus: "transfer", "we are", "beneficiary", "account", "the beneficiary", "details".
counterfactuals: Ignoring the wording entirely and judging on structure alone, confidence would be 30.8% instead of 1.4%.

rules_fired.reason: short, linkless payment request carrying executive authority or secrecy framing

response_plan: Freeze any outbound payment referencing this thread and confirm the request by a phone number already on file — never one from the email.
Search the mail estate for other messages from the same sender or reply-to address in the last 30 days.
Check whether the spoofed executive's real mailbox shows a new forwarding rule or unfamiliar sign-in.
